_doc: Each Night City district's look (DistrictLook), from its look tags in data/world/city.json and the book's description (docs/world/nc_<id>.md; page in `why`). Applies to gigs in that district on scenes without a theme of their own (neighbourhood/street scenes, lone buildings). Theme keys (SceneTheme.of: same meaning as themes.json): palette, neon (sign hues), lamp (street-lamp colours: light warmth), lamp_keep, blaze, fire, ambient, surround, mats, plus light (greybox LOOKS overrides: ambient/amb_e/key/key_e/fog/fog_d/sky/rim/lights/fog_*), walls (per-building facade colour pool by wall material: {colors, pattern, scale}), signs (0-2: neon sign density, 0 = none), grime (0-2: street litter and overhead cables). Generator keys (DistrictGen): ruin (0-1: building decay, replaces the profile's; rubble on the streets), height (-1..2 floors on the profile's buildings; the scene grows taller to fit), green (0-1: street trees and more parks), props (0-2: street furniture density) with street (its pieces), cars (0-2: parked-car density) with optional wrecks (0-1 share), mix (lot uses added to the profile's mix weights). Real-world principles only (European old towns, Chinatown night markets, gated estates, ruined cities, seaside resorts, smog-belt industry).

little_europe.why: NC2045 p.54-55: crumbling brick blocks beside new towers, small blue-collar businesses and pubs; old-town principle: brick and stone, deco trims, warm lamps, cobbles

little_china.why: NC2045 p.96-97: half rebuilt (bamboo scaffolding, Petrochem resin), half war zone; Chinatown night-market principle: signs stacked on every facade, red and gold, stalls in the street, steam

kabuki.why: NC2045 p.200-201: one of the cleanest, richest districts, built by Night City's Japanese community; Tokyo entertainment-street principle: clean pale facades, white-and-pink signs, food stalls, lanterns

executive_zone.why: NC2045 p.232-233: walled, gated enclave of the richest few, manicured lawns, guarded estates; gated-estate principle: white walls, lawns and trees, cool security lighting, almost no signs, no litter

charter_hill.why: NC2045 p.224-225: a suburb of identical houses and fake lawns patrolled by Militech; postwar-suburb principle: one beige house after another, lawns, quiet lamps, few signs

downtown.why: NC2045 p.80-81: working-class district fighting gentrification: old businesses, goth clubs and day markets under new towers; old-downtown principle: mixed brick and glass, club signs, busy pavements

hot_zone.why: NC2045 p.90-91: ruins of the old corporate centre coated in cancer dust; unstable towers, sinkholes, falling glass; no City Manager, no power; bombed-city principle: rubble everywhere, gutted towers, fires, no neon

pacifica_playground.why: NC2045 p.276-285: Southside pleasure district of casinos, brothels and parties, pulled back from blight; seaside-resort principle: faded pastel stucco, boardwalk planks, palms, casino neon over sea mist

playland.why: NC2045 p.302-313: a 24/7 theme-park resort with drones, rides, a boardwalk and a fake forest; amusement-park principle: candy colours, every surface lit, trees and kiosks, swept paths

heywood_industrial_zone.why: NC2045 p.256-257: factories, warehouses and depots under the worst smog in the city; smog-belt principle: yellow haze, sodium lamps, oily grey-ochre concrete, barrels and pallets, few signs

heywood_docks.why: NC2045 p.240-241: a mob-run port for small cargo ships: cranes, containers and rail behind guarded fences; harbour principle: cold sea fog, sodium floodlights, crates and pallets

port_of_night_city.why: NC2045 p.150-151: the city's main sea gate, run by sea nomads: harbour, cranes, container stacks, rail yard; harbour principle: sea fog, floodlights, cargo everywhere

new_westbrook.why: NC2045 p.212-213: an old suburb turned refugee camp: split conapts, cube-hotel strip malls, flickering ad screens; refugee-camp principle: low cramped blocks, tarps and stalls, litter, cold screen light

norcal_military_base.why: NC2045 p.178-181: a sovereign military enclave of barracks, hangars and checkpoints under Military Police; base principle: brutalist olive-grey concrete, white floodlights, barriers and sandbags, parade lawns, no signs

north_heywood.why: NC2045 p.246-247: working-class sprawl of cube hotels and empty factories beside shiny corporate campuses; strip principle: a neon strip over tired blocks

old_combat_zone.why: NC2045 p.166-167: the flattened San Morro Industrial Zone rebuilt by refugees into a warren of shored-up buildings and fortresses; post-war principle: patched ruins, sandbags, burning barrels, half the lamps dead

old_japantown.why: NC2045 p.128-129: liquefied ground and fallout drove the rich out; faded Japanese signs, pastel corporate blocks, gang-war graffiti; abandoned-district principle: faded pastels, dim and broken signs, dust

outskirts.why: NC2045 p.294-301: badlands, cracked roads, wind turbines and dust storms around the city; desert-edge principle: sunset dust, sand-coloured ground, few lamps, no neon to speak of

rancho_coronado.why: NC2045 p.286-293: a corporate beaverville gutted in the war: ruined suburb, tent cities, dead malls, dust; ruined-suburb principle: low broken houses, dead lawns, dust haze, dark streets

reclamation_zone.why: NC2045 p.158-159: rail nomads' young district: rail yards, converted train cars, junk heaps, busy workshops; rail-yard principle: work lights, junk piles, crates, chop shops

santo_domingo.why: NC2045 p.264-273: suburb turned refugee camp turned nomad stronghold: patchwork shanty roofs, containers, food trucks, dust; nomad-camp principle: low patchwork blocks, stalls, warm fires, dusty light

south_night_city.why: NC2045 p.138-139: the Island's oldest combat zone of abandoned warehouses, shanty towns and container housing under smog; slum principle: dark streets, trash heaps, dead lamps, scattered signs

the_glen.why: NC2045 p.114-117: the new seat of government: civic monuments, glass towers, constant construction, heavy policing; civic-centre principle: pale stone and glass, plazas and lawns, cool white light, barriers

university_district.why: NC2045 p.104-105: a walled, armed campus of brown brick and geodesic domes with student bars around it; campus principle: brown brick, quads and trees, warm lamps

upper_marina.why: NC2045 p.66-67: a fast-gentrifying waterfront of galleries and quick-build towers under a corp megastructure; marina principle: fresh white and pastel blocks, cool sea air, cafe furniture

watson_development.why: NC2045 p.186-187: the boomtown: new megabuildings, factories and crowded conapts built with Japanese co-prosperity money; boomtown principle: tall new blocks, construction, dense Japanese-style signage
